root_cause.text: A race condition in `unix_stream_bpf_update_proto()` where the `unix_peer(sk)` pointer is read without holding the unix state lock, allowing a concurrent `unix_release_sock()` to set it to NULL and free the peer socket, leading to a use-after-free when `sock_hold()` is called on the stale pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description provides the exact race sequence: CPU0 (bpf iterator) calls `sk_pair = unix_peer(sk)` then CPU1 (close) calls `unix_peer(sk) = NULL; sock_put(skpair)` before CPU0 does `sock_hold(sk_pair)`, which accesses freed memory. The patch adds `unix_state_lock(sk)` and `unix_state_unlock(sk)` in `bpf_iter_unix_seq_show()` to protect this access.
